# Expert report — Paid acquisition (search/social -> assessment)

I have enough current data across search, social, local, and pre-launch viability. Writing the report now.

# Paid Acquisition for SMD Services — Channel Read & Playbook

_Skeptical-expert briefing. Bottom line up front: **paid is the wrong first dollar for SMD today, and the second or third dollar at best.** Keep it on the radar, wire the plumbing, but do not turn the spend on until the assessment funnel has converted real prospects organically first. The detail below explains exactly why, and what would have to be true to flip the call._

---

## 1. The current playbook as it applies to SMD

Paid acquisition splits into three sub-channels, and they map very differently onto SMD's two-headed offer (Arizona-local consulting + national Operator packs):

- **Paid search (Google Ads, high-intent keywords).** Works when buyers are actively _searching for a solution category_. This is SMD's structural problem: the brief is explicit that owner operational pain is **invisible from the outside and the owner "knows the pain but hasn't articulated the goal."** People who can't name their objective don't type a high-intent query. Nobody searches "managed operator for my title company." They search "hire a virtual assistant," "Clio alternative," or "operations consultant Phoenix" — adjacent, lower-intent, more expensive terms.
- **Paid social (Meta, LinkedIn).** Demand _generation_, not capture — you interrupt someone who wasn't looking. This is theoretically a better fit for invisible pain (you can dramatize the symptom), but it is the slowest-to-convert and most creative-dependent, and it punishes brands with no proof.
- **Local Services Ads / Google Verified (the old Google Guaranteed).** Pay-per-lead, top-of-page, trust-badge product. Tempting for the Arizona consulting side — **but see §4, it largely doesn't fit.**

The 2026 cross-channel reality: an integrated paid+organic motion is the consensus best practice, and **paid's honest job for a pre-launch firm is fast learning (which messages/landing pages convert), not cheap leads.** ([Move Marketing](https://www.move-mktg.com/paid-search-paid-ads-trends-and-predictions-for-2025/), [Bulbul](https://bulbulagency.com/marketing-for-you/when-to-start-paid-ads-for-startups/))

## 2. Concrete tactics SMD could execute

If/when SMD turns this on, these are the specific, defensible moves — ordered by fit:

1. **Arizona-geofenced Google Search, category-not-brand keywords.** Bid on "operations consultant Phoenix," "small business systems consultant Scottsdale," "QuickBooks/CRM setup Phoenix." Tight geo radius around the metro. Send all traffic to `/book` (the single assessment door). This is the most defensible paid play because it captures the rare in-market searcher and the local consulting offer can close in person.
2. **Pack-specific Search for the national Operator, one vertical at a time.** Mirror the pack-standard discipline: a `/packs/law-firm` landing page bidding on "law firm operations / paralegal workflow automation," never generic. One pack live and measured before the next — same Captain-gate logic that governs the packs themselves.
3. **Meta demand-gen against owner-voiced symptoms.** Creative built on the literal symptom lines from the model ("I can't step away," "everything runs on spreadsheets," "our systems don't talk to each other"). Single-symptom-per-ad. The hook is the symptom; the offer is a free assessment. This is the only paid tactic that fits _invisible_ pain.
4. **Retargeting only, before any cold spend.** Pixel the site; retarget visitors who hit `/operator` or a pack page but didn't book. This is the highest-ROI paid dollar at low volume and the safest first test.
5. **LinkedIn for the Operator packs by job title** (owner/managing partner in the 12 verticals). Precise, but expensive — reserve for after Meta proves a message.

What to **avoid**: broad Performance Max (it will spray budget into garbage placements with no conversion signal to optimize against — SMD has _zero_ conversion data, §5), and any "boost post" reflex.

## 3. Benchmarks (external — labeled, not fabricated)

All figures are published third-party benchmarks, not SMD numbers:

- **Overall Google Ads CPL:** ~$70.11 average in 2025, up ~5% YoY (~$66.69 in 2024). ([WordStream](https://www.wordstream.com/blog/2025-google-ads-benchmarks))
- **Business / professional services:** ~$5.58 CPC, ~5.1% conversion, **~$104 cost per lead**; professional-services CPL range commonly cited **$80–$130**. ([PPC Chief](https://ppcchief.com/google-ads-benchmarks/b2b), [First Page Sage](https://firstpagesage.com/reports/average-cost-per-lead-by-industry/))
- **B2B CAC via Google Ads:** commonly **$300–$800** per _customer_ (not per lead). ([Prospeo](https://prospeo.io/s/google-ads-for-b2b))
- **LinkedIn leads:** **$110+** each, materially higher than Search. ([Sopro](https://sopro.io/resources/blog/b2b-cost-per-lead-benchmarks/))
- **Home services search:** ~$7.85 CPC, ~6.37% CTR, ~7.33% conversion (declining YoY), **~$90.92 CPL**; Phoenix CPCs run ~40% higher in summer demand peaks. ([LocaliQ](https://localiq.com/blog/home-services-search-advertising-benchmarks/), [BuiltRight](https://builtrightdigital.com/google-ads-cost-for-home-services/))
- **Minimum budget for Google's algorithm to learn:** ~**$3K–$5K/month** for SMB campaigns — below this you starve the optimizer. ([Get-Ryze](https://www.get-ryze.ai/blog/saas-google-ads-cost-benchmarks-budget-2026))

Read these as the _cost of a raw lead_, not a client. SMD's assessment is a high-consideration sale; a paid lead is several conversion steps from a signed engagement, so true cost-per-engagement is a multiple of the CPL above.

## 4. Honest fit assessment

- **Speed to first lead:** Fast — paid is the _only_ channel that can produce a click within hours. This is its single genuine advantage for a firm under near-term lead pressure.
- **Lead quality / warmth:** **Cold and low-context.** A paid clicker has no relationship, no referral trust, and — critically — must self-diagnose pain that the brief says they _can't articulate._ These are the hardest leads to convert into a paid/serious assessment.
- **What makes it fail for SMD specifically:**
  1. **No proof.** Pre-launch, zero case studies. Paid traffic is unforgiving of an unproven brand; a cold visitor with no social proof and no published price bounces. Referral/networking traffic forgives this; paid does not.
  2. **No conversion data to optimize on.** The engine has _never been pointed at the market and measured_ (139 sends, zero opens/clicks/replies). Modern paid bidding is conversion-signal-driven; with no signal, you're paying Google/Meta to learn what you could learn cheaper organically first.
  3. **Local Services Ads largely doesn't apply.** Google Verified requires industry **licensing + insurance verification** and is built for licensed trades/legal — a generalist solutions-consulting firm isn't a clean category fit, and going live takes weeks of verification. ([Google Support](https://support.google.com/localservices/answer/12174778), [ALM Corp](https://almcorp.com/news/google-local-services-ads-requirements-july-2026/))
  4. **No published pricing** (a voice law) removes the single most common paid-search conversion lever; the ad can't pre-qualify on price, so you pay for unqualified clicks.
- **Near-term vs. compounding:** Paid is **rented, not owned** — it produces leads while you pay and stops the day you stop. For a venture whose moat is _the harness + guide + memory_ and whose Phase-1 distribution is _local relationships_, paid does not compound. Referral and content do.

**The verdict:** paid is a _learning instrument and a scale lever_, not a launch channel. Turning it on now spends scarce pre-launch cash to buy cold, unqualified, proof-starved clicks into a funnel that has never converted a warm one. The binding constraint named in the brief is **close-calls × conversion-per-call, not raw lead volume** — and paid does nothing for conversion-per-call. Worse, flooding an unvalidated funnel with cold paid traffic can _manufacture a false negative_ (the funnel looks broken when really the traffic was wrong).

## 5. Phased ramp (sequence, not calendar)

1. **Prove the funnel organically first.** Run the ~100 ready drafts + referral/networking traffic through `/book`. Get the **first real conversion data** — booked assessments, attended calls, signed engagements. Wire Resend/site analytics so opens, clicks, bookings, and close-calls are actually tracked. _Paid cannot be evaluated until this baseline exists._
2. **Retargeting-only paid, tiny budget.** Once the funnel converts _some_ warm traffic, add a pixel and retarget site visitors who didn't book. Lowest-risk paid dollar; tests creative against an already-interested audience.
3. **One geo-fenced Search campaign, Arizona consulting.** Small daily cap on category keywords → `/book`. Judge it on _cost per booked assessment that shows up_, not CPL.
4. **One Meta symptom-creative test for one Operator pack.** Single vertical, single symptom, demand-gen. Only after a pack page has proven it converts organic traffic.
5. **Scale only the one thing with a positive cost-per-signed-engagement.** Kill the rest. Hold spend at the algorithm-learning floor (~$3–5K/mo per the benchmark) on the survivor; do not spread thin.

The gate between every step is the same: **a measured positive signal at the prior step**, never a date.

## 6. How a paid prospect actually reaches the assessment

Single path, no exceptions, matching the firm-with-flagship / one-front-door structure:

**Ad (category keyword or symptom creative) → pack or `/operator` deep page that names the symptom and the gap → single CTA to `/book` → the voice-capable assessment Operator runs the interview (discloses it's AI, qualifies in conversation, drafts evidence-bound findings) → premium withheld-read report in the portal → Scott joins to deliver the read and close.**

Two non-negotiables: (a) paid traffic lands on a **symptom-matched page**, never the generic home — message-match is the difference between a 7% and a 1% conversion; (b) the **assessment fee acts as the paid-lead qualifier.** Because the fee is credit-back (a pre-payment, not a cost), it filters tire-kickers that cold paid traffic over-produces, protecting Scott's scarce close calendar — exactly the throttle the pricing-as-filter posture intends.
